sources.title: USA and Paraguay 2026 World Cup Preparation and Qualification

evidenceItems.snippet: As a co-host of the 2026 World Cup alongside Canada and Mexico, the United States automatically qualified and did not participate in the CONCACAF qualification rounds.
evidenceItems.summary: USA automatically qualified for the 2026 World Cup as a co-host.

evidenceItems.snippet: Paraguay successfully qualified for the 2026 World Cup, marking their return to the tournament for the first time since 2010. Paraguay finished 6th in the CONMEBOL standings, securing the final automatic qualification spot for South America with 28 points.
evidenceItems.summary: Paraguay qualified for the 2026 World Cup by finishing 6th in CONMEBOL qualifiers.

evidenceItems.snippet: Under head coach Mauricio Pochettino, the U.S. has focused on high-level friendlies to prepare for the tournament. Recent results leading into June 2026 include: May 2026: A 3–2 victory over Senegal. June 2026: A competitive 2–1 loss to Germany. March 2026: Disappointing friendly losses to Belgium and Portugal (combined score of 7–2).
evidenceItems.summary: USA's recent friendly results include a win against Senegal and losses to Germany, Belgium, and Portugal.

evidenceItems.snippet: One of their most significant results was a 2–1 win against Argentina in November 2024, with goals from Antonio Sanabria and Omar Alderete. They maintained a disciplined defensive structure, not conceding more than one goal in any of their final 10 matches leading up to the tournament.
evidenceItems.summary: Paraguay secured a 2-1 win against Argentina in November 2024 and maintained a strong defensive record in their final 10 qualification matches.
